name: terraform init
description: Initialize a working directory: download providers and modules and configure the backend.

flags.description: Upgrade providers and modules to the newest versions allowed by constraints
Supply backend settings from a file or key=value pair (partial backend config)
Ignore existing backend config and reinitialize without migrating state
Copy existing state to a newly configured backend
Skip backend initialization (useful for validate/lint in CI)
Disable interactive prompts

examples.description: Upgrade providers within version constraints and update .terraform.lock.hcl
Move state after changing the backend block

notes: Safe to run repeatedly; re-run after adding providers, modules, or changing the backend.
Commit .terraform.lock.hcl to version control; do not commit the .terraform/ directory.
OpenTofu: every command in this file works with `tofu` in place of `terraform` (e.g. `tofu init`).

name: terraform plan
description: Show the changes Terraform would make to match the configuration, without applying them.

flags.description: Save the plan to a file so apply runs exactly that plan
Set an input variable
Load variables from a .tfvars file
Limit planning to a specific resource or module (escape hatch, not routine use)
Plan to destroy and recreate a specific resource
Create a plan that destroys all managed resources
Plan only to update state to match real infrastructure (drift detection)
Skip refreshing state from real infrastructure
Exit 0 = no changes, 1 = error, 2 = changes present (useful in CI)
Wait for a state lock before failing

examples.description: Save the plan for a later apply
Detect drift between state and real infrastructure

notes: terraform.tfvars and *.auto.tfvars are loaded automatically; other files need -var-file.
Variables can also be set via TF_VAR_<name> environment variables.

name: terraform apply
description: Create, update, or delete infrastructure to match the configuration or a saved plan.

flags.description: Skip the interactive approval prompt
Set input variables (not allowed when applying a saved plan file)
Apply only to a specific resource or module
Force a resource to be destroyed and recreated
Update state to match real infrastructure without changing resources
Limit concurrent operations (default 10)

examples.description: Apply a previously saved plan exactly as reviewed
Plan and prompt for approval interactively
Recreate one resource (replacement for the deprecated taint)

notes: Use -auto-approve only in automation where the plan was already reviewed; it can destroy resources without asking.
Applying a saved plan fails if the state changed since the plan was created.

name: terraform destroy
description: Destroy all resources managed by the current configuration and workspace.

flags.description: Skip the confirmation prompt
Destroy only a specific resource (and its dependents)
Load variables needed to evaluate the configuration

examples.description: Preview a destroy and save it for review

notes: WARNING: Irreversible. Deletes real infrastructure, including databases and buckets, in the selected workspace. Double-check `terraform workspace show` first.
Equivalent to `terraform apply -destroy`.
Add `lifecycle { prevent_destroy = true }` to critical resources as a safeguard.

name: terraform apply -replace
description: Force a resource to be destroyed and recreated; the replacement for the deprecated terraform taint.

examples.description: Preview replacing an indexed resource inside a module

notes: `terraform taint` and `terraform untaint` are deprecated; use -replace instead, which shows the effect in a plan before anything changes.
WARNING: Replacement destroys the existing resource; data on it (disks, local state) may be lost.
Quote addresses containing brackets to avoid shell globbing.

name: terraform fmt
description: Rewrite Terraform configuration files to the canonical format and style.

flags.description: Also format files in subdirectories
Check formatting without writing; exit non-zero if changes are needed
Show formatting differences

examples.description: Format files in the current directory
Fail CI if any file is not formatted

name: terraform validate
description: Check that the configuration is syntactically valid and internally consistent.

flags.description: Output results as JSON

examples.description: Validate in CI without backend credentials

notes: Requires `terraform init` first; it does not contact remote APIs or check credentials.

name: terraform test
description: Run Terraform's native tests defined in *.tftest.hcl files.

flags.description: Run only the specified test file
Print plan or state for each run block

examples.description: Run all tests in the tests/ directory and current directory

notes: Available since Terraform 1.6. Run blocks with `command = apply` create real resources and destroy them afterward, so use a test account.
OpenTofu also supports `tofu test` with the same file format (and *.tofutest.hcl).

name: terraform show
description: Show a human-readable view of the current state or a saved plan file.

flags.description: Output machine-readable JSON

name: terraform output
description: Print output values from the root module state.

flags.description: Print a single string value without quotes (good for scripts)
Print outputs as JSON (shows sensitive values)

examples.description: Get one value for use in a script

notes: Sensitive outputs are hidden in the default view but revealed with -raw or -json.

name: terraform console
description: Open an interactive console for evaluating expressions against the current state.

examples.description: Start the console, then try e.g. cidrsubnet("10.0.0.0/16", 8, 1)

notes: Great for testing functions, locals, and for expressions before writing them in code. Exit with `exit` or Ctrl-D.

name: terraform graph
description: Output the dependency graph of resources in DOT format.

flags.description: Graph type: plan, plan-refresh-only, plan-destroy, or apply

examples.description: Render the graph to SVG with Graphviz

name: terraform providers
description: Show the providers required by the configuration and modules.

name: terraform providers lock
description: Update .terraform.lock.hcl with provider checksums for multiple platforms.

flags.description: Add checksums for a target platform (repeatable)

examples.description: Lock providers for CI and developer machines

notes: Fixes 'provider checksum does not match' errors when the team uses different OS/architectures.

name: terraform state list
description: List resource addresses tracked in the state.

flags.description: Filter by resource ID

name: terraform state show
description: Show the attributes of a single resource in the state.

examples.description: Show a for_each instance (quote the address)

name: terraform state mv
description: Rename or move a resource address in the state without recreating it.

flags.description: Show what would be moved without changing state

examples.description: Move a resource into a module

notes: Prefer declarative `moved { from = ... to = ... }` blocks in code: they are reviewable in plans and work for everyone using the module.
Back up state first (`terraform state pull > backup.tfstate`); a wrong move causes Terraform to plan destroy/create.

name: terraform state rm
description: Stop managing a resource by removing it from state, without destroying the real object.

flags.description: Show what would be removed

examples.description: Forget every resource in a module

notes: WARNING: The real resource keeps existing but is no longer tracked; if it stays in config, the next apply will try to create a duplicate.
Terraform 1.7+ supports a declarative `removed { from = ... lifecycle { destroy = false } }` block as an alternative.

name: terraform state pull
description: Download and print the current state from the backend as JSON.

examples.description: Back up remote state before risky operations

notes: State can contain secrets in plain text; handle backups carefully. `terraform state push` restores a file but can overwrite newer state, so use it only as a last resort.

name: terraform import
description: Bring an existing real-world resource under Terraform management.

examples.description: Import an existing bucket into a resource block you already wrote
With an import block in code, generate matching HCL for the imported resource

notes: Preferred approach (Terraform 1.5+, OpenTofu 1.5+): declare `import { to = aws_s3_bucket.assets  id = "my-assets-bucket" }` in code and run plan/apply; the import is reviewed in the plan.
The resource block must exist (or be generated with -generate-config-out) before importing.

name: terraform force-unlock
description: Manually release a stuck state lock.

flags.description: Do not ask for confirmation

examples.description: Unlock using the Lock ID shown in the error message

notes: WARNING: Only use when you are sure no other Terraform process is running; unlocking during an active apply can corrupt state.

name: terraform workspace list
description: List workspaces; the current one is marked with *.

examples.description: Print only the current workspace name

name: terraform workspace new
description: Create a new workspace with its own separate state and switch to it.

examples.description: Create and switch to a staging workspace

notes: Reference the workspace in code with terraform.workspace. Many teams prefer separate directories/backends per environment over workspaces.

name: terraform workspace select
description: Switch to a different workspace.

flags.description: Create the workspace if it does not exist (Terraform 1.4+)

examples.description: Switch, creating if needed (handy in CI)

notes: `terraform workspace delete <name>` removes a workspace; it refuses if the workspace still tracks resources unless -force is given (which orphans them).

name: terraform login
description: Obtain and save an API token for HCP Terraform (Terraform Cloud) or Terraform Enterprise.

examples.description: Log in to a Terraform Enterprise host

notes: Token is stored in ~/.terraform.d/credentials.tfrc.json. Remove it with `terraform logout`. In CI, use the TF_TOKEN_<hostname> environment variable instead.
